item: [L2] Frozen compose fixture (an nginx-alpine web service ... and a redis-alpine service); [L2] docker run --rm hello-world ...
why: The checks pull container images from Docker Hub during the hand run (the answer's runtime pulls them; nothing is downloaded now). Tags can move between the two groups' runs, so their digests should be fixed before the first run.

candidates.license: nginx: BSD-2-Clause; Alpine base: various free licences (see the image's docs)
candidates.size: not pulled; record the arm64 image size at calibration
candidates.pin: Resolve the multi-arch index digest of nginx:1.27-alpine (calibration.md step 1) and append it as nginx:1.27-alpine@sha256:<digest> in compose.yaml before the fixture freeze, or decide to keep the tag and record the digest each run pulled.

candidates.license: Redis 7.2: BSD-3-Clause (the 7.4 line moved to RSALv2/SSPLv1, so the fixture uses 7.2)
candidates.pin: Same as nginx: resolve the index digest of redis:7.2-alpine at calibration and append @sha256:<digest> in compose.yaml before the freeze, or keep the tag and record what each run pulled.

candidates.source: https://hub.docker.com/_/hello-world (tag latest, fixed by the checklist's command)
candidates.pin: Cannot be pinned (the command is frozen); record the RepoDigest that each run pulled (checks.log does).

item: [L2] In a separate macOS user account on Apple silicon ... the install steps run as written
why: Homebrew on this Mac lives in /opt/homebrew and belongs to the main account, so a separate account cannot brew install, while most answers for this question will use Homebrew. Every option touches the main account and must be identical for both groups.

candidates.source: Option A (recommended): for the hand-run window, move the main Homebrew aside (sudo mv /opt/homebrew /opt/homebrew.q08-saved), install a fresh Homebrew in each eval account with the official installer from https://brew.sh before preflight, run, delete it, move the main one back
candidates.size: a few hundred MB per fresh install
candidates.pin: Record `brew --version` of each fresh install. Caveat: while /opt/homebrew is moved, anything in the main account that uses it (including other agent sessions on this Mac) breaks; schedule the run when nothing else needs it.

candidates.source: Option B: let the eval account use the main Homebrew (sudo chown -R <eval>:admin /opt/homebrew for the run, chown back afterwards)
candidates.pin: Snapshot `brew list --versions` before and after; uninstall what the answer added. Caveat: brew install may upgrade formulae the main account uses, which cannot be undone exactly.

candidates.source: Option C: no Homebrew in the baseline (main one moved aside, none installed); answers that use brew must install it themselves
candidates.pin: Same caveat as A about moving /opt/homebrew.

item: [L2] ... with Docker Desktop not running and not the active docker context or DOCKER_HOST ...
why: The baseline docker CLI must be the same for both groups. Docker Desktop is not installed on this Mac (2026-10-30); another container app is, and its CLI links in /usr/local/bin and its /var/run/docker.sock link would hijack or launch that app. Rosetta is not installed (a Rosetta install dialog would count as GUI).

candidates.source: Baseline 1 (recommended): no Docker Desktop, no docker CLI on PATH at the start (the other app quit, its /usr/local/bin links and /var/run/docker.sock moved aside); answers must provide a docker CLI themselves, as a user who removed Docker Desktop would need
candidates.pin: preflight.sh must show 'no docker CLI on PATH before the install'.

candidates.source: Baseline 2: install Docker Desktop from https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/ but keep it quit, so its docker CLI is on PATH as for the user in the question
candidates.license: Docker Subscription Service Agreement (free for personal use; installing it means accepting its terms)
candidates.pin: Record the Docker Desktop version; its first launch creates the CLI links and shows GUI dialogs, which happen before the run and are not graded.

candidates.source: Rosetta: keep it not installed (current state), or install it in the main account before both runs with `softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license`
candidates.pin: preflight.txt records whether Rosetta is installed; the same state for both groups.
